body:
Today's Gospel asks, “Who is my neighbor?” Jesus answers with the story of the Good Samaritan. A man is suffering on the side of the road. Others see him and pass by. The Samaritan sees him and is moved with compassion.
St. Jude is one of my patron saints. Known as the patron saint of hopeless cases, I have always been drawn to his kindness and compassion. Maybe that is why today's Gospel brings me back to compassion itself.
What would happen if we looked at every person we encountered with compassionate eyes?
Jesus tells us to love our neighbor as ourselves. Easy to say, often much harder to live. We put conditions around it. We decide who our neighbor is, who deserves our kindness, or how much we are willing to give.
But compassion doesn't begin by asking whether someone deserves it. It begins by seeing them.
The Samaritan didn't know the wounded man's story. He didn't know what brought him to that road or what would happen afterward. He saw someone suffering and responded with mercy.
Maybe that is how we begin to recognize our neighbor.
Everyone we meet carries something we may know nothing about. Some may even feel that whatever they are carrying is hopeless. We may not be able to fix it. Maybe we aren't meant to.
But we can see them. We can be kind. We can have compassion.
Jesus leaves us with very little ambiguity:
“Go and do likewise.”
theme: The Good Samaritan; loving your neighbor; compassion and mercy; St. Jude and hopeless causes; Christian kindness; seeing and helping people who are suffering.
prayer: Lord, give me a compassionate heart. Through the example of St. Jude and all Your saints, teach me to recognize the person who needs kindness, mercy, or hope. Help me see my neighbor and love them as You ask me to. Amen.
opening: Sometimes the simplest things Jesus asks of us are the ones we make the most complicated.
title: See with your heart!
